title: Jeff Bezos says AI could power a return to single-earner households as it turbocharges productivity
key_facts: Jeff Bezos told Fox News' Bret Baier on Wednesday evening (7 Oct 2026) that AI-driven productivity means 'you're not going to need to have a two-earner income household'.
He said some people may choose to work three days a week and still support a family.
He said this could make hiring harder for companies.
Business Insider notes Elon Musk has predicted 'universal high income' from AI.
US unemployment has stayed between 4.1% and 4.5% over two years; a June Yale Budget Lab analysis found AI's effect on jobs so far to be modest, changing rather than eliminating jobs.
quote_evidence: If AI increases economic productivity as he expects it to, "you're not going to need to have a two-earner income household," Bezos told Fox News chief political anchor Bret Baier.
"It's going to actually be difficult to hire people because the productivity in the economy is going to make it so that if people don't want to work two jobs, they won't have to."
An analysis by Yale Budget Lab in June this year found that AI's impact on America's job market since it went mainstream in late 2022 has been modest.
why_it_matters_hint: A prominent billionaire's forecast about AI and household work, set against data showing only modest job effects so far.
notes: Full text read. Interview was the evening before the scan window; first reported by Business Insider on 8 Oct.
